paper_sections.title: Reduced Functional Connectivity within the Mesocorticolimbic System in Substance Use Disorders: An fMRI Study of Puerto Rican Young Adults

description.value: The study examined resting-state functional connectivity within the mesocorticolimbic system in Puerto Rican young adults with and without a substance use disorder, and explored associations among connectivity, impulsivity, and SUD.

design.value: Cross-sectional resting-state fMRI study of 28 young adults with and without SUD, using bilateral nucleus accumbens seed-based connectivity, second-level group comparisons, a site moderation analysis, and exploratory impulsivity and path analyses.

description.value: Axial echoplanar images were obtained to provide an effective resolution of 3.75 × 3.75 × 3.5 mm and whole-brain coverage. Two 5-min resting-state scans were obtained for each participant.

Standard image preprocessing methods were used, employing SPM8 Software with the conn_toolbox for functional connectivity analysis. The functional images were slice time and motion corrected, coregistered with a high-resolution anatomical scan, normalized into MNI space, resampled at 2 mm 3, and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm 3 full width at half maximum. Connectivity preprocessing procedures followed the component-based noise correction method to minimize non-neural influences on fMRI signal.

steps.value: Coregistration with a high-resolution anatomical scan
Normalization into Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space
Smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm 3 full width at half maximum (FWHM)

model_settings.value: Resting-state fMRI time series data were correlated voxel by voxel for each participant across the complete resting-time series. Connectivity maps were generated with bilateral nucleus accumbens seed regions, and Fisher z transformation was applied.

Group was the single factor with two levels, SUD+ and SUD−, and comorbid disorders were included as a covariate dummy coded 1 or 0. Motion parameters were included as nuisance regressors at the subject- and group-level. Group comparisons were anatomically restricted to OFC, amygdala, hippocampus, NAcc, and midbrain/VTA regions using masks derived from WFU_pickatlas.
The dependent variable was MCLS connectivity, and the independent variables were Group, Site, and a Group by Site interaction term.
Partial correlations between MCLS connectivity and impulsivity were calculated while controlling for site and group.

The path analysis examined associations between MCLS connectivity, impulsivity, and SUD. The first linear regression model tested impulsivity as associated with low MCLS connectivity; the second tested MCLS connectivity as a predictor of SUD while controlling for impulsivity; bias corrected bootstrapping was used to test the indirect effect.

estimator.value: linear regression and bias corrected bootstrapping
